title: A Summer for the Letters
premise: Ines Thornbury has built a careful life out of other people's words, ghostwriting the memoirs of her ex-fiancé's rival while keeping her own heart safely in past tense. When she needs a date for the Thornbury family reunion at their coastal inn, she hires charming stranger Theo Marsh — never guessing he's the estranged brother of her client, sent to spy on the memoir. As fake affection turns real over one long summer week, Ines must choose between loyalty to her contract and the truth that could free them both. She ends by publishing the memoir under her own name with the truth restored, forgiving herself in the mirror of the inn's old letter room, and choosing Theo — not as an escape from her past, but as part of her future.
about_author: Ines Kavanagh spent a decade writing other people's love stories before daring to write her own. She lives by the sea, where she collects old letters and believes every reunion deserves a second chance.

chapters.title: The Ghost in the Manuscript
chapters.summary: Ines's POV. We meet Ines ghostwriting rival publisher Julian Ashe's memoir, erasing her own voice from every page. A summons to the Thornbury family reunion arrives — the first since her father's death — demanding she bring a partner. Emotional beat: quiet self-erasure and dread, establishing what it costs her to stay invisible.

chapters.title: A Stranger for Hire
chapters.summary: Ines's POV. Desperate, Ines hires Theo Marsh, a warm, watchful man she meets through a friend-of-a-friend, to pose as her boyfriend for the reunion week. Their chemistry is immediate and inconvenient. Emotional beat: guarded hope — she tells herself this is a transaction, but her pulse disagrees.

chapters.title: Arrivals at Saltwind Inn
chapters.summary: Ines's POV. The reunion begins at the family's crumbling coastal inn, full of aunts, old grievances, and her mother's cold appraisal. Theo plays his role too well, charming everyone including Ines's skeptical sister Bea. Emotional beat: belonging almost within reach, and the fear of wanting it.

chapters.title: What Theo Knows
chapters.summary: Theo's POV. Revealed: Theo is Julian's estranged half-brother, sent to learn what the memoir will expose about their family. He justifies the deception even as he falls for Ines over stolen kitchen conversations. Emotional beat: guilt sharpening into love — the reader now knows what Ines doesn't.

chapters.title: Letters in the Attic
chapters.summary: Ines's POV. Sorting her late father's things, Ines and Theo discover a box of unsent letters revealing her father hid a family secret — one Julian's memoir may already contain. They grow closer decoding the past together. Emotional beat: intimacy through shared excavation; memory as both wound and map.

chapters.title: Too Real by Dessert
chapters.summary: Ines's POV. At the reunion's formal dinner, Theo defends Ines against a cruel toast, and the fake relationship tips irrevocably into something true. They kiss in the garden, both forgetting the arrangement entirely. Emotional beat: surrender — joy arriving exactly where she swore not to let it.

chapters.title: The Rival's Chapter
chapters.summary: Theo's POV. Julian arrives unannounced, pressuring Theo for intel and revealing to him how much the memoir will hurt Ines's family. Theo realizes he's become the instrument of the same betrayal he once suffered. Emotional beat: moral crisis — loyalty to blood versus truth to love.

chapters.title: Exposed
chapters.summary: Ines's POV. Bea discovers Theo's identity and forces the truth into the open before the whole family. Ines learns she was a job — and that her father's secret sits in Julian's manuscript, distorted. She sends Theo away. Emotional beat: devastation; every mirror suddenly shows a woman who chose lies again.

chapters.title: The Person in the Mirror
chapters.summary: Ines's POV, with a final Theo section. Alone, Ines confronts her pattern: hiding behind others' words, punishing herself for her father's silence. She rewrites the memoir's final chapter in her own name, telling the whole truth. Theo, having refused Julian's payment, comes back with his own confession. Emotional beat: forgiveness of self first — the climax of the inner arc.

chapters.title: A Summer for the Letters
chapters.summary: Ines's POV. At summer's end, Ines publishes the corrected memoir under her own name, reads her father's last unsent letter aloud to her reunited family, and finds Theo waiting in the letter room. No more past tense. Emotional beat: resolution — belonging chosen openly, love written in her own hand at last.
